title: Digital Kitchener strategy refresh for 2026–2030
subtitle: Development charges hearing for 15 Dellroy Avenue adjourned; digital access, cybersecurity and council updates discussed.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended approval of the refreshed Digital Kitchener strategy, which will guide the City's digital initiatives, priorities and investments from 2026 to 2030 {{vote:m2}}. Staff said the strategy sets direction only. It does not approve vendors, tools or budgets, and any initiative with financial or policy implications will still come back to Council.

Committee members asked about digital literacy, access for residents without devices, cybersecurity awareness, and how often Council will get updates. Staff said they expect at least an annual in-person check-in with Council. One councillor said a motion to expand the computer refurbishment program with the Working Centre is likely to come to the March 23 Council meeting.

The committee also adjourned a development charges complaint hearing for 15 Dellroy Avenue to no later than April 20, 2026, while staff work with the appellant on a possible settlement {{vote:m1}}. A similar complaint for 1438 Highland Road W was removed from the agenda because an appeal had been filed with the Ontario Land Tribunal, so it is no longer within the City's jurisdiction.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the refreshed Digital Kitchener strategy and direct staff to use it to guide digital initiatives, priorities and investments over 2026–2030.
The committee adjourned the Section 20 development charges complaint hearing to a date no later than April 20, 2026, to allow settlement discussions to continue.

debate: Several councillors supported the direction but asked how Council would stay informed. Some said they had not received a full picture of the Innovation Lab's work. Staff acknowledged communication needed improvement and committed to at least annual in-person check-ins plus sharing stories and progress.

One councillor asked for smaller pilots with vendors and ongoing challenges through Pitch Kitchener. The councillor also asked how Council could push staff to take more risks. Staff pointed to pre-market engagement with local vendors and said Council could take part in choosing pitches.

Councillors raised digital access and literacy for residents without devices or internet. Staff said no one will be forced online and that in-person service will stay strong. They also pointed to partners such as the Working Centre, libraries and the University of Waterloo.

On community centre computers and cybersecurity, staff said the machines are heavily used and that staff can only do so much. They said public cybersecurity training is available and the City will keep warning residents about impersonation scams.

One councillor wanted the focus to stay on efficiency and the resources available, and suggested using upgrades already available from existing vendors. Another councillor questioned the references to UN Sustainable Development Goals in the strategy. Staff said they would appear as logos linking back to the corporate strategic plan.
